name: The Roosevelt New Orleans
insider_take: This legendary French Quarter gem has been the heartbeat of New Orleans luxury since 1893, where jazz legends and literary giants once gathered in its opulent halls.
whats_special: The Roosevelt is famously home to the Sazerac Bar, birthplace of America's first cocktail - the Sazerac. The hotel's Blue Room hosted icons like Frank Sinatra and Ella Fitzgerald, while its grand ballrooms have welcomed presidents and celebrities for over a century. The lobby's stunning coffered ceilings and marble columns remain unchanged from its Gilded Age origins.
pro_tip: Book the author's suite where Tennessee Williams penned parts of "A Streetcar Named Desire," and don't miss ordering a Ramos Gin Fizz at the Sazerac Bar - they've been perfecting the 12-minute shake since 1888.
dont_miss: Stroll two blocks to Jackson Square to hear street jazz, visit the historic St. Louis Cathedral, or catch a streetcar on nearby Canal Street. The French Market's legendary café au lait and beignets are just a 5-minute walk away, perfect for experiencing authentic New Orleans culture steps from your luxury retreat.
pros: Historic luxury hotel with grand architecture and timeless elegance
Prime location in the French Quarter within walking distance of major attractions
Exceptional dining options including the famous Sazerac Bar
Impeccable Waldorf Astoria service standards and attention to detail
cons: Premium luxury pricing reflects high-end positioning
Historic building may have older infrastructure in some areas
